how: The starter proposes the logo, supplies its location, reports a tiny version, and receives an explicit offer to join.
Calls seek readers' help making the logo, while related communities' existing logos provide context rather than documented recruits.
The collaboration call receives an explicit offer to join that requests nothing in return.
A proposed expansion receives a brief assent without a reciprocal request.
Anchor coordinates locate the attempt, but a reader also needs a neighbouring logo to find it.
The starter reports an already placed tiny light blue logo at the coordinates while asking for more help.
An edited comment reports that the letters have been made while explaining the retained border.
Participants extend the lettering, choose colours, invite critique of another expansion, and propose alternative spacing and letter colours.
Participants identify individual placers applying opposing blue shades and track another person choosing the darker colour.
When identified placers overwrite competing colours, participants invite them into discussion and promise direct contact to reconcile the work.
The room judges itself unable to defend against a neighbour's anticipated retaliation if expansion takes that neighbour's pixels.
Participants retain the outer black border to avoid consuming the work above them and provoking its makers.
Neighbour restraint here rests on anticipated inability to defend against retaliation, without evidence of a prior negotiated agreement.
Judging an enlarged footprint indefensible supplies the explicit reason for sparing the neighbouring work while keeping the existing mark.
Members thank a maker, praise the logo, exclaim at its image, and celebrate the group effort through the final report.
The final reply records that placement ended and reports a permanent mark intact except for two border pixels.
Acclaim of existing work opens another expansion, and reported completion later becomes the explicit basis for proposing further growth.
Design preferences can continue after placement ends, so proposals require separate evidence of enactment before explaining changes to the canvas.
The starter follows the collaboration call with a progress report at the same coordinates and another request for help.
Starting and calling coincide in the initial proposal, with a later tiny-logo report renewing the request rather than demonstrating a separate starting stage.
An explicit join answers the collaboration call, supporting the response sequence without testing the proposed mechanism of preferred acceptance or silent placing.
Celebration can mark a provisional achievement that immediately invites further expansion rather than a settled final design.
Celebration and fate reporting can occupy the same turn, without demonstrating that marking causes a distinct subsequent preservation activity.
Open critique and informal agreement show drawing choices but cannot establish whether formal organising arrangements existed elsewhere or test a cross-room frequency claim.
A maintenance invitation, preventive border choice, and eventual survival report do not establish actual watching, repairs, or defensive labour.
The room's internal border agreement gives no evidence of reciprocal negotiation or a treaty with the unnamed neighbour.
The visible turns avoid provoking a neighbour and invite colour discussion, leaving attacks on other works unobserved rather than disproved.
Proposing a small mark left of another logo does not identify a lost earlier spot or establish relocation after erasure.
Calling the frozen mark permanent records its fate without documenting a decision to reuse the work or continue organising elsewhere.
Identified colour placers and promised messages establish neither automation nor exclusively manual placement.
Related communities' logos serve as landmarks without documenting exchanged help or reciprocal obligations.
Proximity to related logos does not establish coalition membership or joint defence.
Anticipating a neighbour's attack and declining internal colour fighting do not establish a contest with a rival carried on in talk.
Respecting the work above and choosing a place beside another logo do not demonstrate a host governing a guest mark.
The promised contact targets individual colour placers without establishing an envoy carrying a proposal between rooms.
A collaboration post and deleted-body help title cannot establish whether the host restricted canvas discussion.
The logo call and ambiguous surviving title supply no evidence of the host being restyled or keyed as an April Fools prank.
Related logos and an unnamed neighbour provide no evidence of an inherited quarrel carried onto the canvas.
Brand-colour preferences and an unexplained image exclamation do not establish inherited ideology, lore, political belonging, or allegiance to a colour faction.
The named related communities are landmarks, and the feared neighbour is unnamed, leaving an inherited tie naming an attacked rival unobserved.
Colour discussion and permission to object concern the design without disputing who can commit the room to an agreement with another room.
Reporting two imperfect border pixels does not request cleanup, challenge a preserved version, or contest an account of the event.
Completed letters and a future maintenance invitation do not demonstrate a transition into actual watching or repair.
A preventive border choice supplies neither documented repair pressure nor negotiation with the neighbour.
Restraint has an explicit retaliation rationale, but no reciprocal border agreement establishes the arrow's proposed antecedent.
Maintenance intentions and identified recolourers do not document repair strain leading to scripts or spare accounts.
The final fate report contains no decision to transfer the temporary effort into another purpose or venue.
Anticipated inability to defend newly taken neighbour pixels cannot establish inability to hold the existing spot followed by relocation.
Anchor coordinates and externally linked modular designs do not reveal an agreed pixel template settling the continuing design discussion.
Requests for readers' help do not establish maintenance strain causing help to be sought or received from other rooms.
The internal border choice records neither reciprocal negotiation nor a subsequent exchange of help.
Calls to build are documented, but the explicit decision to avoid provocation supplies no attack call testing the proposed progression.
Neighbour restraint follows an anticipated threat rather than a documented attack call, leaving the attack-refusal mechanism untested.
The internal border agreement records no attack call answered through a truce or a deal with another room.
Concern about possible retaliation does not establish an attack producing rivalry talk.
Neighbour proximity and proposed maintenance provide no sequence from defensive strain to coalition membership.
Visible calls lack evidence of a canvas-post flood or a consequent host intervention.
Internal design agreement and invitations to discuss establish neither inter-room commitment nor a resulting dispute over who may bind the room.
